findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: The ice scoop handle was observed to be in direct contact with the ice in the ice bin at the bar. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the handle to be above the ice. Ensure that the ice scoop handle is always stored above the ice to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The trash can in the kitchen was observed to be in front of and obstructing the only handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the employees. The trash can was moved to another spot. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There were multiple instances where food was observed to be in a package that exposed it to potential contaminants: 

1. There was observed to be mushrooms, cut pineapple and corn dogs stored directly in a grocery bag. CORRECTED- The food items were switched to be in another container.  
2. There was observed to be an open can of tomato purée with the tomato purée still stored inside of it. CORRECTED- The tomato purée was moved into another container. 

Education was conducted with the PIC. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and food should never be stored directly in them. After the can of an acidic food item is opened, the can is no longer meant to protect the integrity of its contents and the food item can be adulterated. Ensure that food is stored in a container that does not expose it to adulteration or to potential contaminants.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT- Inspectors observed that there was a plate of raw chicken above a package of cheese and container of chipotle sauce. CORRECTED - PIC moved the chicken to the bottom shelf. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were two containers of salsa and one container of Birria broth that were observed to be uncovered in the double-door cooler. CORRECTED- The PIC was informed and covered the containers with foil. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by being covered.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them: 

1. The can opener blade. CORRECTED- An employee cleaned this during the inspection. 
2. The top of the baffle in the ice machine. A follow up is scheduled for 11/13/2026 to ensure that the ice machine baffle has been cleaned. 

Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The double-door standing cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 46F. The following TCS food items were probed and voluntarily discarded: 

1. A container of sour cream that probed to be at 46F. 
2. A container of chicken that probed to be at 46F. 
3. A container of refried beans that probed to be at 48F. 
4. A container of birria broth that probed to be at 46F. 

The other TCS food items that probed to be at 45F or under were moved to a preparation cooler. The facility has space in both preparation coolers to store all of their TCS food items in. A follow up is scheduled for 11/9/2026 to ensure that the cooler has been repaired and is properly cold holding at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There is a waste water leak coming from the pipes under the handwashing sink and under the triple sink. The triple sink waste water leak appears to be coming from both the pipes and from the bottom of the wash basin. A follow up is scheduled for 11/9/2026 to ensure that these leaks have been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to allow sewage to be properly conveyed.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink in the kitchen is observed to need to be re-sealed to the wall. Ensure that the sealing is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment:
The following personal items were observed to be mixed in with items intended for the facility: 

1. There was observed to be a personal jacket on a shelf in dry storage touching and above items for the facility. 
2. A half gallon of milk that was in the bar cooler. 
3. Open can of jalapeños observed to be in the bottom of the preparation cooler mixed in with items for the facility. 

Discussed getting a tub or bucket and labeling it personal for employees to place their personal items in. Ensure that personal storage is in an area that does not expose food, equipment, linens, and single-service items to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There is tomato purée in the bottom of the preparation cooler that is observed to still be in the open can. Tomato purée is acidic and should not continue to be stored in the can after it is opened, as it can contaminate the tomato purée. The facility did not have another container to transfer the tomato purée to, as there are not enough containers for all of their food. A follow up is scheduled for 8/26/2026 to ensure that there are enough containers for food to be stored in to prevent contamination to food.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There are no lids observed for the steam table to protect and cover the food. Lids are also useful for trapping the heat to allow for proper hot holding. A follow up is scheduled for 8/26/2026 to ensure that lids have been obtained for the steam table. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by storing it in covered containers.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: There was not a CFPM present at the start of the inspection and there were a number of priority and priority foundation violations observed during the inspection, including but not limited to: no sanitizer bucket made and available, switching tasks without washing hands and changing gloves, improper storage order, and improper reheating procedures. CORRECTED- The CFPM arrived during the inspection and these violations were corrected during the inspection. The CFPM was observed to educate staff on these violations. Based on this number of priority and priority foundation violations, an educational visit will be conducted with the Spanish translator at SCDPH, Kelly Hamlin.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: A Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was not present at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to switch from washing a dish to engaging in food preparation. CORRECTED- The PIC educated the employee on when to wash their hands. Ensure that staff are educated on when to wash hands and on proper handwashing procedures. Further education will be conducted regarding handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.

In the same cooler, there was also observed to be raw sirloin tip on top of a pan of cooked meat. CORRECTED- The raw eggs and the raw sirloin tip were moved to be on the bottom shelf of the cooler, below other ready-to-eat food items. A storage order handout that is in Spanish was provided and an English one is already posted on a cooler. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.

Saran Wrap is observed to be used to cover some of the containers and it was recommended continue this practice with all of them. Ensure that food is stored in a package, a covered container, or is wrapped to protect the food from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.comment: There was a pan of cheese sauce that was probed to be at a temperature of 97F on the steam table. The employees stated that it was being reheated on the steam table. CORRECTED- The PIC and the employees were educated that reheating should be done on the grill or the stove to make sure that the food item reaches a temperature of at least 165F. The cheese sauce was placed on the stove to be reheated. The probe thermometer was observed to still be in the package and the PIC was educated that this should be in use to make sure the reheated food is reaching the correct temperature. Steam tables are not typically made to be able to rapidly reach a temperature of 165F, which is why they should not be used for reheating. Ensure that food is being reheated to at least 165F before being placed in hot holding.
findings.citation_text: 3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of cheese sauce, a container of cooked meat, and a pan of cooked meat that were observed to not have any date-marking on them. CORRECTED- The employee stated that the food items were made yesterday and the foods were date-marked. Date-marking was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods that are kept for more than 24 hours are date-marked with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day. Further education will be conducted regarding date-marking.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The bleach that was being used to make sanitizer buckets was observed to be a bleach that is not EPA-Registered and is meant for “whitening and brightening”. CORRECTED- The Disinfecting, EPA-Registered Clorox Bleach was in the dry storage room and was shown to the PIC to use for sanitizing food-contact surfaces. Ensure that chemicals used for sanitizers are EPA-Registered and are safe to use on food-contact surfaces. Ensure that staff are educated on this.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There was not a sanitizer bucket made and available for use in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that staff are educated that a sanitizer bucket should be made before engaging in food preparation or cooking.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink in the kitchen is observed to need to be re-sealed to the wall.
2. The bare wood above the triple sink needs to be painted or sealed. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There were not signed employee reporting agreements available for any of the employees. The PIC was given copies in both Spanish and English. A follow up is scheduled for 3/13/2026 to ensure that all employees have signed an employee reporting agreement. Ensure that once all employees have signed an agreement, that these are kept in a safe, accessible place to be shown for all future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
The following improper storage order was observed in the facility: 

1. A plate of raw chicken over a pan of raw chorizo. CORRECTED- The raw chicken was moved to be below the raw chorizo. 
2. There was a cold holding unit that the PIC stated should be a freezer. The PIC explained that it has not been freezing correctly. The unit was observed to be approximately 31F to 35F during the inspection. There was observed to be raw beef, raw chicken, and raw chorizo above cooked chicken and produce in this cold holding unit. All raw beef chicken, and chorizo items in the unit were moved to be on the bottom shelf to protect the other food items in the unit from contamination. 

Storage order was discussed with the PIC and a handout in both Spanish and English was given to the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.

Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer in the facility that can measure the temperature of both cold and hot food items.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(E) Temperature Measuring Devices.
